correctness.rationale: For every integer m>=1 and all 2m+1 independent nonnegative weights of sum one, lambda_max is convex and lambda_2 is concave, so automorphism averaging weakly improves width. For equal pendant weights a and bridge b=1-2ma, the two extremal eigenvalues are the roots of lambda^2-((m+1)a+2b)lambda+2ab, giving strictly convex squared width 4-(12m+4)a+(9m^2+10m+1)a^2. Its constrained minimizer gives the exact three regimes. Equality in the convex averaging is sharpened by a common top eigenvector when b>0; when b=0, componentwise star Rayleigh equalities force equal conductances and equal budgets. Thus every optimizer, not merely one symmetrized optimizer, is unique. Standalone verifier: 1550 assertions, exact rational cases, symbolic polynomial and full-matrix eigenspectra; finite checks support, not prove, the all-size theorem.

value.rationale: The optimized difference between the largest and second-smallest Laplacian eigenvalues is a published graph-network design objective with SDP/embedding interpretation. The balanced double star isolates a natural bottleneck between two identical star communities. Its all-integer unique optimum changes from a positive central bridge at m=2 (1/57) to an exactly zero central bridge for every m>=3. The exact support transition and unrestricted-weight rigidity give a structural counterpoint to spectral-gap design (which values connectedness), not a numerical table recomputation or a generic eigenvalue exercise. The result is confined to its stated topology and objective and does not claim faster actual consensus.
